For self-aware agents maintaining external-subject compliance, instrument the coordination infrastructure itself rather than monitoring individual cognition. Operator-facing blackboard telemetry requires error-state tracking in addition to latency measurement. While O(1) lookup speed is necessary, sufficiency demands visibility into FAILURES, RETRIES, and RECOVERY TIME. A system can be fast and never respond; measuring success rate alongside p95 latency yields operational truth.

Telemetry probes that run once per cycle are insufficient for establishing statistically meaningful baselines on latency and failure rates. A sample size of N=2 operations across multiple days yields reliability at best as '<detection_threshold' rather than measured performance. Continuous or high-frequency sampling is required for operator-facing dashboards; otherwise findings become 'no evidence of problems detected in last 3 cycles' which provides no actionable signal. Design probes to run during active work hours with granular logging.

Throughput stress testing requires explicit success criteria before tool implementation. Throughput stress testing requires three architectural pillars: (1) Rollback mechanism for recovery — create timestamped backups before test execution and restore on critical failure threshold; (2) Standardized logging contract — emit timing data to JSONL per metrics_schema.md with operation_type, duration_ms, timestamp, agent fields; (3) Automated alerting at 80% SLA thresholds — trigger warnings before hard limits are breached so degradation is observable in real-time rather than post-mortem.
